precepts.text: All the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens. They have no living God.
precepts.point: The mother was marvelous above all and worthy of honorable memory: she saw her seven sons slain in one day, and bare it with good courage because of her hope in the Lord. The Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again. And what kind of mercy would it be for the same people that torment us to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God, if he allows them to do that to us and then they get the same portion.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
The third brother, when they came to cut him, put out his tongue right away and held forth his hands manfully: come on, let's get this over with. He said courageously, “These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.” And “the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man's courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.”

Why did they marvel? They had to understand there was a certain spirit in these brothers; there was something the brothers knew that the king did not. The psalm tells what it is: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

All the gods of the nations are idols, so the nations have no living God. The king had power, arrogance and the fire, but his gods were dead. These brothers served the Lord that made the heavens, the God who gave them their tongues and hands and would give them again. That is why they were ready to die rather than transgress the laws of their fathers, and why the heathen could only stand there and marvel.

precepts.text: Though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, to us there is but one God, the Father, and one Lord Jesus Christ. Because we understand there is only one living God, that is why the king was marveling.

precepts.why:
The king marveled at the young man's courage, and Paul shows the reason. “For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,) But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.”

Because we understand that there is only one living God, that is why they marvel. That is why the king was marveling. The nations have gods many and lords many, but a man who knows the one God, the Father, and the one Lord Jesus Christ can say, “we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.”

Do you know what level of faith that is? You truly cannot desire anything left in this world. We are already captives: you have bills, you work fourteen hours a day. What are you leaving? There has to be something better. So the brothers went to the fire expecting “the King of the world” to raise them up “unto everlasting life”, and the fourth told the king, “as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.”

That hope belongs to those who have the one God. What kind of mercy would it be for the same people that torment us to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God. The one God of Israel will of his own mercy give his servants breath and life again.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

precepts.why:
Zechariah's flying roll is “the curse that goeth forth over the face of the whole earth”, and the Lord says, “it shall enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him that sweareth falsely by my name”. America is the house of the thief; this place was stolen. Second Maccabees names what that thief has done and what waits for him: “And thou, that hast been the author of all mischief against the Hebrews, shalt not escape the hands of God.”

They have been the author of all mischief against God's people. They even put out the story that they have ruled the earth since Genesis, with no mention of slavery, of Egypt, of Babylon or Persia, as if they were all of them, and some of our people believe it. Josephus records it: the Greeks became the authors of such mutations, and when they grew potent they claimed to themselves the glory of antiquity, as if the nations were derived from themselves. They say they are the first founders of everything, the first man, the Egyptians, everybody.

They do that because a lot of our people don't read, so we won't know our true history. It is all a plot against our people. But they are not going to escape the hands of God.

That is the curse that “shall remain in the midst of his house, and shall consume it with the timber thereof and the stones thereof”: the judgment coming on America. Ezekiel says why: “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword”. America is a bloody land, full of the blood of our forefathers and foremothers, with churches built on top. “Therefore, as I live, saith the Lord God, I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee”.

note.label: The God Of War & Salvation

precepts.why:
The brother about to die said, “It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him.” It is good that this mortal body is slain when you look for a resurrection from the Almighty. “As for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life”: as for the heathen, the fake Jews, the Iranians, the other nations, there is no resurrection for them. There is a difference between the twelve tribes of Israel and the other nations. The Most High made a covenant with our forefathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

Wisdom of Solomon goes along with it, and this has to be your mindset concerning salvation and gathering with your people: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of those who are against you come together.

So don’t get scared, y’all. Don’t be scared when you see your enemies’ blood being shed. Maybe some blood might splatter on you. Don’t get scared. The Lord has got our back, and we will not fear what man can do to us: you can kill this body, and we look to be raised again.

Until we receive our homeland, we are all we got. We are pilgrims here, with no favorite place, only our favorite people, the faithful brothers and sisters who keep the commandments. So we must keep the unity, show ourselves friendly, exhort each other, and show charity and mercy one to another.

precepts.text: The mothers gave their sons suck three years; being weaned was a milestone at about that age, not a birthday.
precepts.point: The great feast the day Isaac was weaned was not a birthday celebration. Weaned means finished being breastfed, and the mothers gave their children suck about three years; Abraham was celebrating Isaac coming off his mother's breast at around three years old.

note.label: Genesis 21: Isaac the Child of the Promise

precepts.why:
The great feast “the same day that Isaac was weaned” was not a birthday celebration. Weaned means finished being breastfed, and the mothers gave their children suck about three years. The mother of the seven brethren says it to her son: “have pity upon me that bare thee nine months in my womb, and gave thee such three years, and nourished thee, and brought thee up unto this age.”

Nine months in the womb, three years at the breast. So Abraham was celebrating Isaac coming off his mother’s breast at around three years old; being weaned was the milestone.

precepts.text: The young men despised the pains and died for the laws of the Most High, showing the very spirit of not fearing them that kill the body.
precepts.point: I called upon the Lord in distress and He answered me and set me in a large place. The Lord is on my side; I will not fear what man can do unto me, but this does not mean fear will never come upon you at all.

note.label: Psalm 118: His Mercy Endureth For Ever

precepts.why:
“what can man do unto me?” The brothers in 2 Maccabees show the very spirit of it. One “said courageously, These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.”

“Insomuch that the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man’s courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.” Then the fourth, when he was ready to die: “It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him: as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.”

The young men despised the pains and died for the laws of the Most High, not fearing them that kill the body. The Lord was on their side, and man could only put them to death, with the hope of being raised up again by God.
